scope: All current repository treatment entities. Fifteen source-complete launch profiles are published; six incomplete current records remain in review.
publication_rule: Null means the field could not be supported responsibly. Published records have a minimum comparison profile and claim-level sources; uncertainty is stated rather than filled by inference.

treatments.summary: Injectable botulinum toxin products that temporarily reduce the activity of targeted facial muscles.
treatments.primary_purpose: Commonly used to soften the appearance of movement-related facial lines.
treatments.name: Neuromodulators

treatments.summary: Injectables that work gradually through a tissue response rather than representing one interchangeable product.
treatments.primary_purpose: Commonly used where a gradual change in facial fullness or skin quality is the goal.
treatments.name: Collagen stimulators

treatments.summary: A broad class that includes radiofrequency, ultrasound, and other energy-delivery devices with device-specific clearances and protocols.
treatments.primary_purpose: Commonly used for skin tightening, lifting, resurfacing, or coagulation goals without injectables.
treatments.name: Energy-based devices

treatments.summary: A prescription botulinum toxin type A product.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved for the temporary improvement in the appearance of moderate to severe glabellar lines associated with corrugator and/or procerus muscle activity in adult patients.
treatments.name: Xeomin

treatments.summary: A prescription botulinum toxin type A product.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved for the temporary improvement in the appearance of moderate to severe glabellar lines associated with corrugator and/or procerus muscle activity in adult patients.
treatments.name: Daxxify

treatments.summary: A specific Restylane hyaluronic-acid filler product; its profile remains in review until the full US/Canada and clinical field set is completed.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved for cheek augmentation and correction of age-related midface contour deficiencies in patients over 21, with other product-specific indications documented in its current labelling.
treatments.name: Restylane Lyft
Botox Cosmetic
treatments.summary: A prescription botulinum toxin type A injection that temporarily reduces selected expression lines by weakening targeted muscle activity.
treatments.primary_purpose: Temporary improvement of specified dynamic facial and neck lines in adults; approved US cosmetic areas are product-label specific.
treatments.mechanism: Binds to motor nerve terminals and inhibits acetylcholine release by cleaving SNAP-25, producing temporary chemodenervation of injected muscles.
treatments.what_it_changes: Movement-driven lines and the pull of specifically injected muscles.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not add tissue volume, replace structural support, fill a hollow, or resurface skin.
treatments.tightening_level: None; any contour change comes from altered muscle pull, not tissue tightening.
treatments.result_timing: An effect can begin within 1 to 2 days and commonly strengthens during the first week.
treatments.sessions_text: One treatment visit; repeat treatment is considered after the effect wanes and should follow the product label.
treatments.downtime_text: No required recovery period is specified in the label, although injection-site effects can occur.
treatments.longevity_text: The FDA label describes approximately 3 to 4 months for glabellar-line effect; individual areas and patients vary.
treatments.reversibility: Not immediately reversible; the effect usually diminishes as neuromuscular function recovers.
treatments.major_risks: Unwanted weakness such as eyelid or brow ptosis, asymmetry, headache, hypersensitivity, and rare distant spread of toxin effect with swallowing or breathing difficulty. Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to a botulinum toxin preparation or infection at the injection site.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Static etched lines or volume loss can remain even when muscle movement is reduced.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Botox is not a dermal filler and its potency units cannot be converted directly to another botulinum toxin product.
treatments.provider_variables: Muscle assessment, injection sites, dose, depth, symmetry planning, and management of adjacent-muscle spread.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually priced per Botox Cosmetic unit or, less transparently, by treatment area; Botox units must not be converted to Dysport units.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: Targeted, temporary reduction in selected expression lines; it is not a structural facial-volume treatment.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Botox and Dysport share a treatment class but have different labels and non-interchangeable potency units. Botox and fillers are different approaches.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: Do not use with product hypersensitivity or infection at the proposed injection site; additional warnings and patient-specific exclusions require prescriber review.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved prescription biologic for temporary improvement of moderate to severe glabellar lines, lateral canthal lines, forehead lines, and platysma bands in adults under the current US label.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada Drug Product Database lists Botox Cosmetic DIN 02531445 as approved; Canadian indications and dosing must follow the current Canadian product monograph.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for product identity, mechanism, labelled indications, contraindications, and labelled duration; outcomes remain dose-, area-, and patient-dependent.

at_a_glance.onset: Begins in days; builds during week 1
at_a_glance.duration: About 3–4 months for labelled glabellar treatment
at_a_glance.downtime: No required recovery; injection effects possible

treatments.name: Dysport
treatments.manufacturer: Ipsen Biopharmaceuticals; marketed in US aesthetics by Galderma
treatments.summary: A prescription botulinum toxin type A injection used to temporarily improve labelled glabellar lines by reducing targeted muscle activity.
treatments.primary_purpose: Temporary improvement in the appearance of moderate to severe glabellar lines associated with procerus and corrugator muscle activity in adults younger than 65 under the US cosmetic label.
treatments.mechanism: Acts at the neuromuscular junction to inhibit acetylcholine release and temporarily reduce activity in injected muscles.
treatments.what_it_changes: Movement-driven frown lines in the labelled glabellar treatment pattern.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not add volume, replace structural support, or resurface skin.
treatments.tightening_level: None; it modifies muscle activity rather than tightening tissue.
treatments.result_timing: Clinical cosmetic outcomes are assessed after treatment; visible change commonly develops over the first days to two weeks, but individual onset varies.
treatments.sessions_text: One treatment visit; the US label states treatment should not occur more frequently than every three months.
treatments.downtime_text: No formal recovery period is specified, but injection-site reactions and unwanted weakness can occur.
treatments.swelling_text: Localized swelling can occur after injection.
treatments.longevity_text: Temporary; the US label limits retreatment frequency to no more often than every three months rather than promising an exact duration for every patient.
treatments.reversibility: Not immediately reversible; effects generally diminish as neuromuscular function recovers.
treatments.major_risks: Eyelid ptosis, headache, injection-site reactions, hypersensitivity including to cow's-milk protein, infection-site contraindication, and rare distant spread of toxin effect with swallowing or breathing difficulty.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: The US cosmetic indication is narrower than Botox Cosmetic's current label, and static lines or volume loss may persist.
treatments.marketing_misconception: A Dysport unit is not equivalent to a Botox unit and no direct unit conversion should be presented.
treatments.provider_variables: Label-appropriate patient selection, dose, injection pattern, anatomy, symmetry, and spread into adjacent muscles.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually priced per Dysport unit or by area; raw Dysport-unit prices must remain separate from Botox-unit prices.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: Temporary reduction of labelled glabellar-line severity, not facial volumization.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Same broad treatment class as Botox, but product potency units, labelling, dose, and clinical plan are not interchangeable.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to any botulinum toxin product or cow's-milk protein and with infection at the proposed site; prescriber review is required for other warnings.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved prescription biologic for temporary improvement of moderate to severe glabellar lines associated with procerus and corrugator activity in adult patients younger than 65.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada Drug Product Database lists Dysport Aesthetic DIN 02387735 as marketed; use must follow the current Canadian product monograph.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for product identity, labelled indication, dose-frequency limit, contraindications, and non-interchangeability; comparative onset or superiority claims are not established here.

at_a_glance.onset: Develops over days; assess over roughly 2 weeks
at_a_glance.duration: Temporary; retreat no more often than every 3 months
at_a_glance.downtime: No formal recovery; injection effects possible

treatments.name: Hyaluronic acid dermal fillers
treatments.summary: A class of injectable gels that add or restore volume; each product is approved or licensed for specific tissues, depths, and treatment areas.
treatments.primary_purpose: Product-specific correction or augmentation of approved facial or hand areas by adding gel volume.
treatments.mechanism: An implanted hyaluronic acid gel occupies space in soft tissue; formulation, cross-linking, concentration, particle properties, and injection plane differ by product.
treatments.what_it_changes: Volume, contour, projection, and selected folds or hollows when an appropriately indicated product is placed in the intended tissue plane.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not reduce muscle contraction like a neuromodulator and is not a skin-resurfacing treatment.
treatments.tightening_level: No direct tissue-tightening action; contour support can create a lifted appearance in selected anatomy.
treatments.result_timing: Volume change is visible immediately, with assessment refined after early swelling settles.
treatments.sessions_text: Often one visit with possible staged treatment or touch-up; amount and number of sessions depend on product, area, and goal.
treatments.downtime_text: Usually limited social downtime, but swelling, tenderness, redness, and bruising can be conspicuous for days and sometimes longer.
treatments.swelling_text: Common and product/area dependent; lips can swell substantially.
treatments.longevity_text: Product- and area-specific. FDA consumer guidance gives roughly 6 to 12 months for many absorbable HA fillers, while some approved products have longer study follow-up.
treatments.reversibility: Many HA fillers can often be reduced with clinician-administered hyaluronidase, but this use is off-label in the US, response varies, and complete reversal is not guaranteed.
treatments.major_risks: Swelling, bruising, pain, tenderness, lumps, infection, inflammatory reactions, and rare inadvertent intravascular injection causing tissue necrosis, vision loss, or stroke.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: The wrong product, amount, or placement can look overfilled, fail to address the actual cause, or require more than one syringe.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Dermal fillers are not one interchangeable product and are structurally different from Botox.
treatments.provider_variables: Diagnosis, product selection, injection plane, amount, cannula or needle choice, vascular safety technique, and complication readiness.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: Filler is not selected by skin tone alone, but bruising, inflammation, and post-inflammatory pigment change may present differently; product labelling and injector experience still matter.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually priced per syringe or mL; price comparisons must retain product, syringe volume, area, and whether multiple syringes are expected.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: From subtle lip or line correction to structural contour change, depending on product and total volume.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: HA fillers may be substitutes only when two specific products are intended for the same area and plane. They are a different approach from Botox.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: Avoid when product contraindications apply, at infected or inflamed sites, or when the goal requires muscle relaxation, skin resurfacing, or surgery rather than volume.
treatments.fda_status: The FDA approves dermal fillers product by product and for specific indications; the HA-filler class itself is not a single approved product.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada licenses HA filler devices product by product through MDALL for Class III devices; class-level status does not establish a licence for every brand or indication.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for class mechanism, product-specific regulatory model, common reactions, and vascular risk; duration and suitability must remain product- and area-specific.

at_a_glance.reversibility: Often reducible with off-label hyaluronidase; not guaranteed

treatments.name: Juvéderm
treatments.summary: A family of hyaluronic acid fillers with product-specific formulations and approved treatment areas.
treatments.primary_purpose: Product-specific facial augmentation or correction across cheeks, chin, temples, jawline, lips, perioral lines, folds, and infraorbital hollowing.
treatments.mechanism: Cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel adds physical volume; rheology, concentration, cross-linking, lidocaine content, approved plane, and intended area differ by product.
treatments.what_it_changes: Product-dependent volume, projection, contour, and selected folds or hollows.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: The family name does not identify one formulation, one indication, one duration, or a neuromodulator effect.
treatments.tightening_level: No direct tightening; contour support may look lifting in selected cases.
treatments.result_timing: Immediate gel volume, followed by reassessment after injection-related swelling.
treatments.sessions_text: Usually one visit per area with possible staged treatment or touch-up; product and volume are individualized.
treatments.downtime_text: Typically limited, but swelling, bruising, tenderness, redness, firmness, and lumps may occur.
treatments.longevity_text: Varies by the specific Juvéderm product, treatment area, amount, and patient; family-wide duration claims are not used.
treatments.reversibility: The HA gel may often be reduced with off-label hyaluronidase, but response is product dependent and not guaranteed.
treatments.major_risks: Injection-site reactions, lumps or nodules, infection, inflammatory reactions, and rare intravascular injection with necrosis, vision loss, or stroke.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Choosing by brand family rather than by the exact product and intended area can create an invalid comparison or mismatched outcome.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Juvéderm is a portfolio, not a single filler with one set of indications or one longevity.
treatments.provider_variables: Specific product, volume, injection plane, anatomy, technique, and management of vascular complications.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per syringe or mL; the exact Juvéderm product and syringe volume must be retained.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Juvéderm and Restylane are comparable brand families, but individual products are substitutes only where indications, area, plane, and desired properties overlap.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: When no product in the family is appropriate for the intended area or when filler contraindications or a non-volume problem applies.
treatments.fda_status: Juvéderm devices are FDA-approved through product-specific PMAs and supplements; the brand family does not have one universal indication.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists active Class III Juvéderm licences, including family and product-specific records; the exact licensed device and intended use must be checked.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for family composition and product-specific regulatory status; family-wide outcome and duration claims are intentionally avoided.

treatments.name: Restylane
treatments.summary: A family of hyaluronic acid fillers whose individual products have distinct formulations, properties, and approved treatment areas.
treatments.primary_purpose: Product-specific augmentation or correction of lips, folds, cheeks, chin, temples, infraorbital hollowing, and dorsal hands.
treatments.mechanism: Cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel adds physical volume; formulation technology, gel properties, lidocaine content, intended tissue plane, and area differ by product.
treatments.what_it_changes: Product-dependent volume, shape, projection, and correction of selected folds or hollows.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: The family is not one interchangeable formulation and does not relax muscles like a botulinum toxin.
treatments.result_timing: Immediate gel volume, with final assessment after early swelling settles.
treatments.sessions_text: Usually one visit per area with possible staged treatment or touch-up.
treatments.downtime_text: Typically limited, but swelling, bruising, pain, tenderness, redness, and lumps can occur.
treatments.longevity_text: Varies by exact Restylane product, area, amount, and patient; no family-wide duration is assigned.
treatments.reversibility: The HA gel may often be reduced with off-label hyaluronidase, with product-dependent and incomplete response possible.
treatments.major_risks: Injection-site reactions, nodules, infection, inflammatory reactions, and rare intravascular injection causing necrosis, vision loss, or stroke.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: A family-level comparison can hide clinically important product and treatment-area differences.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Restylane is a portfolio, not a single filler.
treatments.provider_variables: Specific product, total volume, anatomy, plane, needle or cannula, and complication preparedness.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per syringe or mL; retain the exact product and syringe volume.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Restylane and Juvéderm are comparable families, but individual products are true substitutes only where their intended areas, planes, and goals overlap.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: When filler contraindications apply, the intended area lacks an appropriate product, or the concern is muscular, textural, or surgical rather than volumetric.
treatments.fda_status: Restylane devices are FDA-approved through product-specific PMAs and supplements; each product retains its own indication.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists active Class III Restylane licences, including product-specific records such as Restylane Kysse; exact licensed intended use must be checked.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for family composition, safety framework, and product-specific regulation; no family-wide superiority or duration claim is made.

treatments.name: Juvéderm Voluma XC
treatments.generic_name: cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel with lidocaine
treatments.summary: A hyaluronic acid filler formulated for deep structural augmentation in specific approved facial areas.
treatments.primary_purpose: Deep augmentation for age-related midface volume deficit, chin-profile improvement, and temple hollowing in adults over 21 under the current US labelling.
treatments.mechanism: A 20 mg/mL cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel with 0.3% lidocaine is implanted in product-specific deep tissue planes to add volume and contour.
treatments.what_it_changes: Midface volume, cheek contour, chin projection, or temple hollowing when used in the corresponding labelled plane.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It is not a lip-specific filler, does not relax facial muscles, and does not tighten skin directly.
treatments.tightening_level: No direct tightening; structural volume can change contour.
treatments.result_timing: Volume change is immediate; touch-up assessment in pivotal studies occurred after early swelling, commonly at weeks rather than the same day.
treatments.sessions_text: One initial treatment with possible touch-up according to the labelled area and study protocol.
treatments.downtime_text: Injection-site responses are common and may last days to weeks.
treatments.swelling_text: Common; severity and duration vary by area and technique.
treatments.exercise_restrictions: The patient labelling advises minimizing strenuous exercise and extensive sun or heat exposure for the first 24 hours or until initial swelling and redness resolve.
treatments.longevity_text: Cheek clinical-study benefit was evaluated through up to 24 months; this is not a promise that every treatment or newly approved area lasts 24 months.
treatments.reversibility: May often be reduced with off-label hyaluronidase, but complete or immediate reversal is not guaranteed.
treatments.major_risks: Swelling, tenderness, firmness, lumps, bruising, redness, infection, inflammatory reactions, and rare intravascular injection with necrosis, visual impairment, or stroke.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Using a structural cheek/chin/temple filler for a lip goal is an intended-area mismatch; one syringe may also be insufficient for bilateral structural correction.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Voluma and Restylane Kysse are not like-for-like products merely because both are HA fillers.
treatments.provider_variables: Area-specific plane, amount, facial proportions, injection technique, and vascular anatomy.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: The US labelling reports study enrollment across Fitzpatrick skin types; this does not eliminate individual risk of bruising, inflammation, or pigment change.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per 1 mL syringe; total cost depends on area and number of syringes.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: Structural, area-dependent contour change rather than fine surface-line smoothing.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Not a true substitute for Restylane Kysse because their labelled intended areas differ; the comparison is educational and area mismatch must remain visible.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: Not appropriate for lip augmentation under this profile or when filler contraindications, infection, severe allergy history, or a non-volume concern applies.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved by PMA supplements for cheek augmentation for age-related midface volume deficit, chin augmentation, and temple hollowing in adults over 21.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists Juvéderm Voluma with lidocaine under active Class III medical-device licence 77899.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for formulation, labelled areas, contraindications, adverse events, and pivotal-study follow-up; individual durability and required volume vary.

at_a_glance.duration: Cheek study follow-up up to 24 months

treatments.name: Restylane Kysse
treatments.generic_name: cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel with lidocaine
treatments.summary: A flexible hyaluronic acid filler approved in the US for lip augmentation and upper perioral lines.
treatments.primary_purpose: Add fullness to the lips and correct upper perioral rhytids in adults over 21.
treatments.mechanism: Cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel with lidocaine is injected into lip or upper-perioral tissue to add temporary volume and smooth selected lines.
treatments.what_it_changes: Lip fullness, definition, and selected upper-lip lines.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It is not intended in this profile for cheek, chin, or temple structural augmentation and does not relax muscles.
treatments.result_timing: Volume is visible immediately; assessment should allow early lip swelling to settle.
treatments.sessions_text: One initial treatment with optional touch-up as clinically appropriate.
treatments.downtime_text: Lip-site reactions are very common; swelling, tenderness, bruising, lumps, and firmness may remain visible for days and sometimes longer.
treatments.swelling_text: Very common after lip injection; most trial diary symptoms resolved within about two weeks.
treatments.longevity_text: In the FDA pivotal study, 60% of subjects were responders at week 48; this does not guarantee one-year correction for every patient.
treatments.reversibility: May often be reduced with off-label hyaluronidase, but response is variable and complete reversal is not guaranteed.
treatments.major_risks: Swelling, bruising, tenderness, pain, lumps, infection, inflammatory reactions, and rare intravascular injection with necrosis, vision impairment, or stroke.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Swelling can temporarily exaggerate the result, and the product is not designed to replace structural cheek or chin augmentation.
treatments.marketing_misconception: A one-year study responder rate is not the same as a guaranteed one-year result.
treatments.provider_variables: Lip anatomy, amount, symmetry, injection plane, technique, and management of vascular compromise.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: The pivotal study included a Fitzpatrick-skin-type subgroup analysis; individual bruising and pigment response can still vary.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per 1 mL syringe; half-syringe or promotional pricing must remain separate.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Not a true substitute for Voluma because the products have different labelled intended areas and structural goals.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: Not appropriate for the Voluma-profile cheek, chin, or temple goals; avoid when label contraindications or active infection apply.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved under PMA supplement P140029/S021 for lip augmentation and correction of upper perioral rhytids in patients over 21.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists Restylane Kysse under active Class III licence 95283.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for formulation, labelled area, pivotal-study outcomes, and safety; long-term response remains individual.

treatments.name: Sculptra
treatments.summary: An injectable poly-L-lactic acid biostimulator used in a staged series for gradual correction of labelled facial wrinkles and folds.
treatments.primary_purpose: Correction of shallow to deep nasolabial-fold contour deficiencies, fine lines and wrinkles in the cheek region, and other facial wrinkles in immunocompetent adults under the US aesthetic labelling.
treatments.mechanism: PLLA microparticles produce a local tissue response associated with gradual collagen deposition; initial water-related fullness subsides before the treatment effect develops.
treatments.what_it_changes: Gradual tissue support and correction of selected facial wrinkles or contour deficiencies.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not provide the same predictable immediate gel contour as an HA filler and is not used in the lip vermilion or periorbital area under the IFU.
treatments.adds_volume: Gradually, through biostimulation rather than a persistent HA gel bolus.
treatments.tightening_level: No device-like tightening; gradual collagen response may improve support.
treatments.result_timing: Most clinical-study participants saw results by about one month; improvement develops gradually.
treatments.sessions_text: Average 2 to 3 sessions over several months; typical treatment is three sessions at least 3 to 4 weeks apart.
treatments.downtime_text: Injection-site swelling, tenderness, redness, pain, bruising, bleeding, itching, and lumps can occur.
treatments.swelling_text: Common initially and can temporarily mimic correction before subsiding.
treatments.longevity_text: The current manufacturer summary and cheek clinical program report sustained improvement for up to two years; individual response varies.
treatments.reversibility: Not enzymatically reversible like an HA filler; effects and adverse nodules may be difficult to correct.
treatments.major_risks: Injection reactions, papules or nodules including delayed inflammatory nodules, granuloma, infection, and intravascular injection with infarction or embolic phenomena.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Early post-injection fullness fades, results are gradual, and a multi-session course may be required.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Sculptra is not an immediately shapeable HA filler and 'collagen stimulation' does not make it risk-free or reversible.
treatments.provider_variables: Reconstitution, hydration time, dilution, injection plane, distribution, session spacing, massage instruction, and avoiding overcorrection.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per vial; compare the number of vials per session and the planned number of sessions.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: Gradual, diffuse correction rather than a sharply localized immediate contour.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Sculptra and Radiesse both have biostimulatory effects but differ in material, immediate volume, reversibility, technique, and labelled uses.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: Contraindicated with ingredient hypersensitivity or a history of keloid formation or hypertrophic scarring; not for lip vermilion or periorbital injection under the IFU.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved by PMA and supplements for specified facial contour deficiencies and wrinkles, including the 2023 cheek fine-line and wrinkle indication.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists Sculptra under active Class III licence 71658.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for indication, treatment course, safety, and two-year cheek-study follow-up; aesthetic response and vial needs vary.

at_a_glance.onset: Gradual; often visible by about 1 month
at_a_glance.downtime: Injection swelling/bruising; nodules can be delayed

treatments.name: Radiesse
treatments.treatment_class: Calcium hydroxylapatite dermal filler and biostimulator
treatments.generic_name: calcium hydroxylapatite microspheres in an aqueous gel carrier
treatments.summary: An injectable calcium hydroxylapatite filler that provides immediate gel-carrier volume and a longer tissue response around resorbable microspheres.
treatments.primary_purpose: Correction of moderate to severe facial wrinkles and folds, selected lower-face or jawline contour indications under current product labelling, and correction of dorsal-hand volume loss.
treatments.mechanism: Calcium hydroxylapatite microspheres suspended in a gel carrier provide immediate fill; the carrier dissipates as tissue forms around the microspheres, which are gradually resorbed.
treatments.what_it_changes: Immediate volume and structural contour in approved tissue planes, with a subsequent tissue response.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not relax muscles and cannot be dissolved with hyaluronidase like an HA filler.
treatments.tightening_level: No device-like tightening; structural support and diluted off-label uses must not be conflated with labelled correction.
treatments.result_timing: Immediate volume, followed by evolution as the carrier dissipates and tissue response develops.
treatments.sessions_text: Often one treatment with individualized amount; additional treatment depends on area, response, and label.
treatments.downtime_text: Swelling, bruising, redness, pain, itching, and tenderness can occur; hand and facial recovery differ.
treatments.longevity_text: FDA consumer guidance describes calcium hydroxylapatite filler effects as approximately 18 months; individual product, area, and patient results vary.
treatments.reversibility: Not dissolvable with hyaluronidase; correction of unwanted placement can be difficult.
treatments.major_risks: Injection reactions, nodules, infection, material visibility or palpability, and rare intravascular injection with necrosis, visual loss, or stroke.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Immediate correction can evolve as the carrier dissipates, and unwanted product cannot be simply enzymatically dissolved.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Radiesse is not interchangeable with Sculptra or HA filler; hyperdilute protocols may be off-label and should not redefine the approved product profile.
treatments.provider_variables: Product version, dilution if any, plane, area, amount, anatomy, and complication management.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per 1.5 mL syringe; retain syringe volume, product version, area, and any dilution protocol.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: Immediate structural correction with a subsequent tissue response.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Overlaps with Sculptra in some broad goals but differs in immediate volume, composition, injection plan, reversibility, and labelled indications.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: When a reversible HA option is required, the desired area is not in the product labelling, or product contraindications or active infection apply.
treatments.fda_status: FDA-approved by PMA and supplements for product-specific facial and hand indications; current Radiesse (+) labelling must be checked for the exact area.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists active Class III licences for Radiesse (78893) and Radiesse (+) (95140).
treatments.evidence_grade: High for composition, approved-use framework, immediate filler action, and serious risks; off-label dilution outcomes are not generalized.

at_a_glance.duration: Approximately 18 months in FDA class guidance

treatments.name: Thermage FLX
treatments.summary: A noninvasive monopolar radiofrequency platform that heats tissue while cooling the skin surface.
treatments.primary_purpose: Noninvasive treatment of wrinkles and rhytids within the device's cleared indications; cosmetic 'lifting' language should be understood as modest tissue contraction/remodelling rather than surgery.
treatments.mechanism: Delivers 6.78 MHz monopolar radiofrequency energy to produce controlled tissue heating and selective coagulation while contact cooling protects the epidermis.
treatments.what_it_changes: May produce gradual, modest smoothing or tightening through thermal tissue contraction and remodelling.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not add filler volume, paralyze muscles, remove large skin excess, or reproduce a surgical facelift.
treatments.result_timing: Manufacturer materials describe gradual change over roughly 2 to 6 months.
treatments.sessions_text: Commonly marketed as one treatment; repeat treatment is individualized and not guaranteed by clearance.
treatments.downtime_text: Usually no planned downtime, but transient redness, swelling, soreness, or contour symptoms can occur.
treatments.bruising_text: Not a typical treatment effect, but individual reactions vary.
treatments.longevity_text: Manufacturer materials describe results lasting about 1 to 2 years; independent evidence is heterogeneous and individual response varies.
treatments.reversibility: Not reversible; delivered thermal injury cannot be withdrawn.
treatments.major_risks: Pain, erythema, swelling, burns, blisters, scarring, pigment change, altered sensation, nodules, and contour irregularity; electrical implants are an important contraindication in device instructions.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Improvement can be subtle or absent and should not be compared with surgical lifting.
treatments.marketing_misconception: FDA clearance for device indications is not proof of a facelift-equivalent result.
treatments.provider_variables: Tip, pulse count, energy, treatment vectors, tissue contact, cooling, anatomy, and recognition of excessive heating.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: Radiofrequency is not chromophore-targeted, but burns and post-inflammatory pigment change remain possible; settings and operator experience matter.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per session, treatment area, and pulse/tip plan; face, eyes, neck, and body prices are not interchangeable.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: Subtle-to-moderate noninvasive change in selected patients.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Thermage FLX and Ultherapy are different energy modalities with overlapping broad goals, not identical treatments.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: Not for someone expecting surgical correction; device instructions flag implanted electrical devices and require assessment of skin and medical contraindications.
treatments.fda_status: Thermage FLX received FDA 510(k) clearance K170758 for device-specific noninvasive indications including treatment of wrinkles and rhytids; clearance is not an approval of every marketing claim.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists Thermage FLX under active Class III licence 112966; older Thermage CPT records also exist.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for device identity and regulatory mechanism; moderate and heterogeneous for magnitude and durability of cosmetic tightening.

at_a_glance.downtime: Usually none planned; thermal reactions possible

treatments.name: Ultherapy
treatments.generic_name: microfocused ultrasound system with real-time imaging
treatments.summary: A noninvasive microfocused-ultrasound platform that images tissue and deposits focal thermal-coagulation points at selected depths.
treatments.primary_purpose: Device-specific noninvasive lifting of brow and lax submental and neck tissue and improvement of décolletage lines under US clearances.
treatments.mechanism: Real-time ultrasound imaging guides microfocused ultrasound energy to create discrete thermal-coagulation points at selected tissue depths, initiating a wound-healing and collagen-remodelling response.
treatments.what_it_changes: May produce modest, gradual lifting or tightening in selected areas.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not add volume, remove skin, relax muscles, or equal a surgical facelift.
treatments.result_timing: Manufacturer and clinical literature describe change developing over about 2 to 3 months and continuing up to 6 months.
treatments.sessions_text: Often one treatment in manufacturer protocols; additional treatment depends on response and clinical plan.
treatments.downtime_text: Usually no planned downtime; transient erythema, edema, tenderness, bruising, welts, or altered sensation can occur.
treatments.longevity_text: Published reviews report improvement assessed out to roughly one year, while manufacturer materials say a year or longer; durability varies.
treatments.pain_level: Published systematic reviews describe moderate treatment discomfort on average, with substantial patient and protocol variation.
treatments.reversibility: Not reversible; deposited thermal-coagulation points cannot be removed.
treatments.major_risks: Pain, redness, swelling, bruising, welts, transient numbness or weakness, burns, scarring, and contour change; correct depth and anatomy are critical.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: The measured lift is generally modest and may not be visible enough for someone seeking surgical-level change.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Treatment at a deep support layer is not equivalent to surgically repositioning that layer.
treatments.provider_variables: Imaging, line count, transducer depth, vector planning, energy, tissue coupling, anatomy, and pain management.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: Ultrasound is not melanin-targeted, but injury, burns, and post-inflammatory pigment change can still follow poor technique.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per treatment area and number of lines; full-face, lower-face/neck, brow, and chest quotes should remain separate.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: Modest noninvasive lift in appropriately selected mild-to-moderate laxity.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Overlaps with Thermage in broad goals but uses focused ultrasound rather than monopolar RF and has different depth, discomfort, and planning variables.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: Not appropriate for surgical-level laxity expectations or where IFU contraindications, open wounds, severe acne, or implanted devices in the treatment path apply.
treatments.fda_status: FDA 510(k)-cleared through device-specific submissions including K121700 for brow, submental, and neck lifting and K134032 for décolletage lines.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists the Ulthera System under active Class III licence 79689.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for device identity and cleared indications; moderate for modest efficacy and one-year durability, with heterogeneous protocols.

at_a_glance.duration: Evidence commonly follows results to about 1 year

treatments.name: Morpheus8
treatments.summary: A fractional radiofrequency device that inserts an array of electrodes into tissue and delivers RF energy at selected depths.
treatments.primary_purpose: Dermatologic and surgical procedures requiring electrocoagulation, hemostasis, or contraction/coagulation of soft tissue within the device's cleared parameters.
treatments.mechanism: Programmable needle electrodes penetrate tissue and deliver fractional bipolar radiofrequency, creating discrete zones of thermal coagulation at selected depths.
treatments.what_it_changes: May remodel texture, scars, and laxity through combined needle injury and thermal coagulation; exact use depends on tip and settings.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not add filler volume and its 510(k) clearance does not establish superiority over other RF-microneedling devices.
treatments.tightening_level: Potentially modest to moderate, highly protocol and patient dependent.
treatments.result_timing: Early treatment effects evolve over weeks to months as healing and remodelling occur.
treatments.sessions_text: Often delivered as a series, but a universal session count is not established by the FDA clearance; protocol depends on indication and settings.
treatments.downtime_text: Redness, swelling, crusting, pinpoint bleeding, tenderness, and temporary track marks can occur; deeper or higher-energy treatment can extend recovery.
treatments.reversibility: Not reversible; needle and thermal injury cannot be withdrawn.
treatments.major_risks: Pain, bleeding, infection, burns, pigment change, scarring, fat loss, contour change, nerve injury, and disfigurement. FDA issued a 2025 safety communication about serious complications reported with certain RF-microneedling uses.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Device branding can obscure how strongly depth, energy, passes, tip, and provider judgment determine both result and risk.
treatments.marketing_misconception: FDA clearance for coagulation/contraction uses is not a blanket clearance for every advertised wrinkle, scar, fat-remodelling, or tightening claim.
treatments.provider_variables: Needle depth, coated versus uncoated tip, energy per pin, pulse duration, passes, overlap, treatment endpoint, anatomy, anesthesia, and infection control.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: The K231790 clearance limits energy above 62 mJ per pin to Fitzpatrick skin types I–IV. Lower-energy treatment still requires individualized settings and pigment-risk counselling.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per session and treatment area; package prices must be normalized to a per-session equivalent without mixing promotions.
treatments.expected_result_magnitude: Variable; depends more on protocol and indication than on device name alone.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Morpheus8 and Potenza share an RF-microneedling category but differ in cleared language, tips, energy delivery, and protocols.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: When the patient cannot accept thermal-injury risks, has active infection or impaired healing, or expects a result outside the supported device indication.
treatments.fda_status: FDA 510(k)-cleared, including K231790, for specified dermatologic and surgical electrocoagulation, hemostasis, and soft-tissue coagulation/contraction uses; high-energy use has a Fitzpatrick-type limitation.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists active Class III InMode fractional RF device licences that include Morpheus8 configurations; exact model and handpiece should be verified.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for device mechanism, clearance boundaries, and current FDA safety warning; lower and heterogeneous for aesthetic protocol, session count, and durability.

at_a_glance.downtime: Redness/swelling and surface reaction for days

treatments.name: Potenza
treatments.summary: A radiofrequency microneedling platform with multiple monopolar/bipolar and insulated/non-insulated tip configurations.
treatments.primary_purpose: Dermatologic and general surgical procedures for electrocoagulation and hemostasis under the US clearance; advertised cosmetic protocols go beyond that narrow cleared wording.
treatments.mechanism: Microneedle electrodes enter tissue and deliver monopolar or bipolar radiofrequency through selected insulated or non-insulated tip configurations, producing controlled coagulation.
treatments.what_it_changes: Can create fractional needle and thermal injury used in clinician-directed resurfacing or remodelling protocols.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not add volume, and the US clearance does not itself establish a wrinkle, acne-scar, or tightening indication.
treatments.tightening_level: Potentially modest to moderate in aesthetic protocols, but not established as a specific FDA-cleared outcome.
treatments.result_timing: Remodelling, if achieved, develops over weeks to months rather than immediately.
treatments.sessions_text: Often used in a series, but no universal session count is established by the US clearance.
treatments.downtime_text: Redness, swelling, tenderness, pinpoint bleeding, crusting, and temporary needle marks can occur.
treatments.reversibility: Not reversible; thermal and needle injury cannot be withdrawn.
treatments.major_risks: Pain, bleeding, infection, burns, scarring, pigment change, fat loss, contour change, and nerve injury; the FDA's 2025 RF-microneedling safety communication applies to the procedure category.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: Many public claims describe cosmetic outcomes that are not the same as the device's narrow US cleared indication.
treatments.marketing_misconception: The number of modes or tips does not by itself prove superior results or safety.
treatments.provider_variables: Tip selection, insulated status, monopolar or bipolar mode, depth, energy, pulse duration, passes, overlap, anesthesia, and infection control.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: RF is not melanin-targeted, but burns and post-inflammatory pigment change remain possible; no equivalence across all skin tones is inferred from clearance.
treatments.pricing_basis: Usually per session and treatment area; packages should be converted only when the included area and session count are explicit.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Same broad device category as Morpheus8, but different hardware, tips, cleared wording, and protocol choices prevent simple equivalence.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: When active infection, impaired healing, implanted-device concerns, or unwillingness to accept thermal injury makes treatment unsuitable; exact IFU screening is required.
treatments.fda_status: FDA 510(k)-cleared under K192545 for dermatologic and general surgical procedures for electrocoagulation and hemostasis. The clearance should not be rewritten as an FDA-cleared wrinkle or skin-tightening indication.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists Potenza Fractional RF Microneedle Electrosurgical Unit under active Class III licence 106699.
treatments.evidence_grade: High for device identity, mechanism, and regulatory boundaries; limited for product-specific comparative efficacy, session count, and durability.

at_a_glance.downtime: Redness/swelling and surface reaction for days

treatments.name: HydraFacial
treatments.generic_name: powered dermabrasion with suction and fluid delivery
treatments.summary: A branded superficial facial procedure combining powered exfoliation, suction-based extraction, and topical solution delivery.
treatments.primary_purpose: Temporary improvement in surface cleansing, exfoliation, hydration, and cosmetic appearance.
treatments.mechanism: A handheld tip uses controlled suction and fluid flow to exfoliate the stratum corneum, remove surface debris, and deliver topical solutions.
treatments.what_it_changes: Surface debris, temporary hydration, smoothness, and visible radiance.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not add structural volume, relax muscles, tighten deep tissue, or produce surgical or injectable-level contour change.
treatments.result_timing: Surface smoothness and hydration are typically assessed immediately after treatment.
treatments.sessions_text: One session for a temporary surface effect; repeat or maintenance frequency is elective and not a durable regulatory claim.
treatments.appointment_time: Common branded protocols are approximately 30 minutes, with longer deluxe protocols possible.
treatments.downtime_text: Usually no planned downtime, though transient redness, sensitivity, irritation, or breakout can occur.
treatments.swelling_text: Not expected as a routine effect; stop and assess unexpected swelling.
treatments.bruising_text: Not expected with routine settings, but excessive suction can mark fragile skin.
treatments.reversibility: The superficial exfoliation is not reversible, but the cosmetic hydration effect is temporary.
treatments.major_risks: Irritation, redness, sensitivity, abrasion, suction marks, infection if hygiene is inadequate, and reaction to topical solutions; device and solution contraindications must be screened.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: The immediate glow is superficial and temporary and will not correct laxity, muscle-driven lines, scars, or volume loss.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Infusing topical serum during a facial is not equivalent to injecting filler or delivering a deep tightening treatment.
treatments.provider_variables: Tip, suction level, number of passes, solution choice, skin-barrier assessment, hygiene, and whether add-ons change the procedure.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: Avoid overly aggressive suction or exfoliation in anyone prone to post-inflammatory pigment change; no universal skin-tone outcome is inferred.
treatments.pricing_basis: Per session and protocol tier; Signature, Deluxe, Platinum, boosters, and packages must remain distinct.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Broadly comparable with DiamondGlow for a surface facial goal, but the handpieces, exfoliation method, and topical-delivery systems differ.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: When the skin barrier is compromised, there is active infection or inflammatory disease, a solution allergy is present, or the goal requires deeper medical correction.
treatments.fda_status: No HydraFacial-branded PMA, De Novo, or 510(k) indication was identified in this review; do not describe the cosmetic facial itself as FDA approved. Device model registration and exemption status are model-specific.
treatments.canada_status: Health Canada MDALL lists HydraFacial microdermabrasion systems under active Class II licence 79154 and a handpiece licence 79395; exact model and intended use should be verified.
treatments.evidence_grade: Moderate for device process and short-term surface effects; limited for durable clinical outcomes and no longevity claim is published.

treatments.name: DiamondGlow
treatments.treatment_class: Diamond-tip dermabrasion with suction and topical infusion
treatments.generic_name: powered dermabrasion with simultaneous suction and topical delivery
treatments.summary: A branded superficial facial procedure using a reusable diamond tip, suction, and simultaneous delivery of topical Pro-Infusion solutions.
treatments.primary_purpose: Temporary surface exfoliation, extraction, and topical infusion for smoother, brighter-looking skin.
treatments.mechanism: A diamond-tip handpiece abrades the superficial stratum corneum while suction removes debris and the device delivers a selected topical solution.
treatments.what_it_changes: Superficial texture, debris, and temporary hydrated appearance.
treatments.what_it_does_not_change: It does not add structural volume, relax muscle activity, tighten deep tissue, or replace scar resurfacing.
treatments.result_timing: Surface cosmetic change is assessed immediately after treatment.
treatments.sessions_text: One session for temporary surface improvement; repeat treatments are elective and durability is not established here.
treatments.appointment_time: The manufacturer describes a treatment of approximately 30 minutes.
treatments.downtime_text: Usually no planned downtime, although redness, sensitivity, abrasion, suction marks, or reaction to topical products can occur.
treatments.swelling_text: Not expected routinely; unexpected swelling warrants assessment.
treatments.bruising_text: Not expected routinely, but excessive suction can mark fragile skin.
treatments.reversibility: Superficial exfoliation is not reversible; the cosmetic hydration effect is temporary.
treatments.major_risks: Irritation, erythema, abrasion, suction marks, infection if hygiene is inadequate, and reactions to topical solutions; contraindications in the user manual must be followed.
treatments.most_likely_disappointment: A polished immediate appearance is temporary and does not correct deep wrinkles, laxity, muscle pull, or volume loss.
treatments.marketing_misconception: Topical infusion during dermabrasion is not injectable delivery into deep tissue.
treatments.provider_variables: Diamond-tip grit, suction, passes, pressure, solution choice, hygiene, and skin-barrier assessment.
treatments.skin_tone_notes: Aggressive abrasion can provoke post-inflammatory pigment change in susceptible skin; conservative technique and barrier assessment matter.
treatments.pricing_basis: Per session and protocol; full-face, body, add-on, package, promotion, and membership prices must remain separate.
treatments.true_substitute_notes: Broadly comparable with HydraFacial for a superficial facial goal, but uses diamond-tip abrasion rather than HydraFacial's proprietary vortex-style tip and fluid path.
treatments.when_not_appropriate: When there is active infection, open or compromised skin, significant inflammatory disease, solution allergy, or a goal requiring deeper treatment.
treatments.fda_status: The underlying SilkPeel/Dermalinfusion powered-dermabrasion device family is FDA-listed as Class I under product code GFE and described in FDA records as 510(k)-exempt; this is not FDA approval of every DiamondGlow cosmetic claim.
treatments.canada_status: No DiamondGlow-named Class II–IV active MDALL licence was identified. Class I devices do not receive an MDALL device licence, so Canadian establishment and model status require separate verification.
treatments.evidence_grade: Moderate for device process and immediate surface effects; limited for durable outcomes, and no longevity claim is published.
